FNS_PaneTypeRegistry.help: Before each project save, re-check this registry: update entries whose component moved, drop entries whose component is gone, and republish a host that initialised before the global registry existed. Off skips the sweep for this registry only.

FNS_PaneTypeRegistry.name: Viewreadme
FNS_PaneTypeRegistry.label: View Readme
FNS_PaneTypeRegistry.help: Open the PaneTypeRegistry developer README as a styled markdown annotate in this network (uses the bundled md viewer).

FNS_PaneTypeRegistry.name: Openauthor
FNS_PaneTypeRegistry.label: Link
FNS_PaneTypeRegistry.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

FNS_Remote.name: Active
FNS_Remote.label: Active
FNS_Remote.help: Bind the server and serve this session. Off = nothing listens.

FNS_Remote.name: Port
FNS_Remote.label: Port
FNS_Remote.help: First port of the span to bind (20 ports from here).

FNS_Remote.name: Boundport
FNS_Remote.label: Boundport
FNS_Remote.help: The port actually bound.

FNS_Remote.name: Lan
FNS_Remote.label: Lan
FNS_Remote.help: OFF = loopback only (127.0.0.1). ON = every interface, so phones on your Wi-Fi can reach it. Deliberate act: leave it off unless you want the LAN to see this session.

FNS_Remote.name: Status
FNS_Remote.label: Status
FNS_Remote.help: One line of current state.

FNS_Remote.name: Url
FNS_Remote.label: Url
FNS_Remote.help: Pairing URL (loopback). Carries the access token in the fragment.

FNS_Remote.name: Openpairing
FNS_Remote.label: Open Pairing Page
FNS_Remote.help: Open the pairing page (QR + link) in your browser.

FNS_Remote.name: Regeneratetoken
FNS_Remote.label: Regenerate Token
FNS_Remote.help: Mint a new access token. Every existing link stops working.

FNS_Remote.name: Maxtouches
FNS_Remote.label: Maxtouches
FNS_Remote.help: How many simultaneous touches to expose as CHOP slots.

FNS_Remote.name: Flipy
FNS_Remote.label: Flipy
FNS_Remote.help: Browser Y counts DOWN from the top; TouchDesigner counts UP from the bottom. On = convert to TD's convention.

FNS_Remote.name: Normalize
FNS_Remote.label: Normalize
FNS_Remote.help: On = 0-1 across the touch area. Off = multiply back up by the phone's reported screen size in pixels.

FNS_Remote.name: Createtarget
FNS_Remote.label: Createtarget
FNS_Remote.help: Where the builder pulses below drop their operators. Blank = the network you have open.

FNS_Remote.name: Createselectchop
FNS_Remote.label: Create Select CHOP
FNS_Remote.help: Build a Select CHOP pointed at the touch channels.

FNS_Remote.name: Createselectdat
FNS_Remote.label: Create Select DAT
FNS_Remote.help: Build a Select DAT pointed at the client table.

FNS_Remote.name: Createreceiver
FNS_Remote.label: Create Receiver
FNS_Remote.help: Build one COMP holding both, ready to drag anywhere.

FNS_Remote.name: Controlstatus
FNS_Remote.label: Controlstatus
FNS_Remote.help: What is currently exposed to the remote.

FNS_Remote.name: Exposeperform
FNS_Remote.label: Expose Perform Window
FNS_Remote.help: Expose the perform window's own custom parameters to the remote.

FNS_Remote.name: Performwindow
FNS_Remote.label: Perform Window
FNS_Remote.help: Blank = the project perform window.

FNS_Remote.name: Performpages
FNS_Remote.label: Perform Page Filter
FNS_Remote.help: Space-separated page names to expose. Blank = all custom pages.

FNS_Remote.name: Performpars
FNS_Remote.label: Perform Parameter Filter
FNS_Remote.help: Space-separated parameter names/patterns. Blank = all.

FNS_Remote.name: Control0comp
FNS_Remote.label: Component
FNS_Remote.help: A COMP whose custom parameters the remote may see and drive.

FNS_Remote.name: Control0pages
FNS_Remote.label: Page Filter
FNS_Remote.help: Space-separated page names to expose. Blank = every custom page.

FNS_Remote.name: Control0pars
FNS_Remote.label: Parameter Filter
FNS_Remote.help: Space-separated parameter names or patterns. Blank = all.

FNS_Remote.name: Control0enable
FNS_Remote.label: Active
FNS_Remote.help: Uncheck to hide this block from the remote without clearing it.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Comp
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Widget COMP
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Panel COMP published as the toolbar widget. Defaults to the parent component.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Canonicalname
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Canonical Name
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Unique name for this widget in the global toolbar registry.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Callback
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Callback DAT
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Optional DAT with toolbar callbacks for this widget.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Autoregister
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Auto-register
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: When on, keep this widget published into the global toolbar registry while this component exists.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Register
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Register
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Publish once into the global toolbar registry, even if Auto-register is off.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Unregister
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Unregister
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Take this tool's contribution back out of the registry and turn Autoregister off, so it stays out. Register puts it back.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Regstatus
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Registration Status
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Read-only status of this host registration.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Menuorder
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Toolbar Order
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Preferred order among registered widgets, managed by the global registry. -1 = no preference (append at the end).

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Displayed
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Displayed
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Default visibility of the widget in the toolbar (managed by the global registry).

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Barwidth
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Bar Width
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Width of this widget in the toolbar. 0 = auto (follow the widget). Persisted here; the registry writes manager edits back.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Barheight
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Bar Height
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Height of this widget in its zone. 0 = the zone's own row height. The registry sizes the SOURCE panel to this, because a mirror is a window onto the widget, not a scaler -- an oversized source shows only its top-left corner in the slot.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Zone
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Timeline Zone
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Which part of TD's timeline this widget is published into. 'Transport row' appends it after the native play/stop controls. 'Properties block' places it in the left 279px column. 'Background strip' spans the full width in the frame-ruler band and is drawn UNDERNEATH the ruler -- the ruler's own background is transparent, so it shows through.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Helpurl
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Help URL
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: The tool's wiki/help page opened from the Configurator (right-click the Name cell). Leave empty to auto-discover from a docsHelper COMP (its Url par) inside the registered panel or its parent.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Promotepars
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Promote Parameters
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: When on, the host mirrors its key Registration parameters onto the parent tool as a bound 'Registry' page. Turn off before shipping a tool that should not expose registry controls.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Presaveheal
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Pre-Save Heal
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Before each project save, re-check this registry: update entries whose component moved, drop entries whose component is gone, and republish a host that initialised before the global registry existed. Off skips the sweep for this registry only.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Scope
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline Scope
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Which timeline these tools act on. 'Root' is the global timeline at /local/time. 'A component's local timeline' targets the Time COMP at <Scope Comp>/local/time -- TD's Component Time, which has its own play state, rate and range.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Scopecomp
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Scope Comp
FNS_TimelineTools.help: The component whose local timeline to act on, used when Timeline Scope is set to 'A component's local timeline'. Leave empty to fall back to the root timeline.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Ensurelocal
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Add Component Time
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Give Scope Comp its own local timeline if it has none, by creating <comp>/local/time cloned from /sys/local/time -- the same thing TD's right-click 'Add Component Time' does.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Moviefile
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Movie File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Video to load. Optional -- audio alone is fine, as is both.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Audiofile
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Audio File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Audio to load. Optional. Also what FNS_Waveform draws, so setting it here is enough -- the waveform follows.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Movieop
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Movie Operator
FNS_TimelineTools.help: A Movie File In TOP to USE instead of loading the file ourselves. Set by dropping one on the tool. While set, that operator is the live source and this tool DRIVES its play mode and index; our own reader stays parked, so the file is never decoded twice. Clear it, or load a file, to go back to our own reader.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Audioop
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Audio Operator
FNS_TimelineTools.help: An Audio File In CHOP to USE instead of loading the file ourselves. Same deal as Movie Operator: while set it is the live source, this tool drives it, and our own reader stays parked.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Movieaudio
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Movie Audio
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What to do when a dropped movie carries embedded audio. 'Ask' offers a menu once per load and remembers nothing; 'Always use it' takes the movie's own audio, in sync with the picture and without reading the file twice; 'Always ignore it' leaves whatever audio you loaded separately alone.

menu.name: ask
menu.label: Ask when the movie has audio

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Loadmedia
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Load Media
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Load Media File now and read back its frame count and rate.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Synclength
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Sync Timeline to Media
FNS_TimelineTools.help: On: the timeline's range is resized to the longest loaded media, so one pass of the timeline is one pass of the media. Off: the timeline is left alone and media longer than it is trimmed to fit instead.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Synctarget
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Sync Length To
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Which medium decides the timeline length when Sync Length is on. 'Longest' is the old behaviour and never truncates anything. 'Ask each time' pops a menu when a movie and audio are both loaded and their durations actually differ -- it stays quiet when there is nothing to decide.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Onmediachange
FNS_TimelineTools.label: On Media Change
FNS_TimelineTools.help:
What happens when the movie or audio file changes.

Ask: a single dialog listing what will be resynced and what it costs, so a long filmstrip bake is never a surprise.
Auto: do all of it silently, including slow bakes.
Manual: load the media only -- press Resync yourself.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Resync
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Resync Everything
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Reload the media, refit the timeline, refit the waveform and rebuild the filmstrip -- the whole chain, in the right order.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Synctimeline
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Sync Timeline to Media
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Set the scoped timeline's rate, start/end and working range to match the loaded media, so one pass of the timeline is exactly one pass of the media.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Followtimeline
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Media Follows Timeline
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Drive the movie's frame index from the scoped timeline instead of letting it play on its own clock. This is what makes a local timeline scrub the media.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Medialength
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Media Frames
FNS_TimelineTools.help: The movie's length in TIMELINE frames (its duration converted through the timeline's own rate, not the file's).

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Mediarate
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Media Rate
FNS_TimelineTools.help: The media file's own frame rate, for information only. It is NEVER applied to the timeline -- the timeline rate is a project decision and no media file overrules it. Lengths are converted through the timeline's rate instead.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Audiolength
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Audio Seconds
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Duration of the loaded audio in seconds. Read-only.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Status
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the last action did, or why it could not. Read-only.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Timelinestrip
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Show In Timeline Strip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Publish this background as the strip behind TD's timeline ruler. Bound to the registry host, so it is the same switch as Autoregister.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Animationeditor
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Also Show In Animation Editor
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Set this background as the Animation editor's Background TOP (/ui/dialogs/keyframer/graph). Unlike the timeline -- where a strip has to be injected into the bar -- the graph has a real background slot, so it fills the whole graph. TD's own value is remembered and put back when this is switched off.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Releasesurfaces
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Release All Surfaces
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Give back every part of TD's UI this package has taken: the timeline strip, the transport controls, the Animation editor background and its controls. Four claims by three different mechanisms -- a single host's Unregister button only ever removed one of them.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Reclaimsurfaces
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Reclaim Surfaces
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Take back exactly what Release All Surfaces gave up -- not everything, so a release is genuinely reversible. With nothing remembered it takes the timeline strip and the transport bar and leaves the Animation editor alone.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlshowfilm
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Filmstrip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the filmstrip in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlfilmopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Filmstrip Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the filmstrip layer in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlshowwave
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Waveform
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the waveform in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlwaveopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Waveform Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the waveform layer in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlslices
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Slices
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How many thumbnails the TIMELINE strip is made of. The strip spans the whole bar and is never zoomed, so it needs far fewer than the Animation editor -- 60 across a 2473px bar is already ~40px per thumbnail.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Stripheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Strip Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How tall the timeline strip is, in pixels -- the bar grows by this much to make room rather than taking it from the transport row. It is also the thumbnail height the timeline strip is decoded at, so changing it rebuilds.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Strip Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How strongly the strip shows through under TD's frame ruler.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlshowmarks
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the marker lines in the timeline strip. Off stops the markers module rendering that view at all, rather than merely hiding it.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlmarkopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Marker Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How strongly the marker lines read in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anshowfilm
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Filmstrip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the filmstrip in the Animation editor.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anfilmopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Filmstrip Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the filmstrip layer in the Animation editor. Separate from the timeline: a background competing with animation curves wants to be fainter than one sitting under a ruler.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anshowwave
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Waveform
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the waveform in the Animation editor.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anwaveopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Waveform Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the waveform layer in the Animation editor.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anslices
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Slices
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How many thumbnails the ANIMATION EDITOR strip is made of. This is what carries detail when the graph is zoomed in, so it wants as many as the texture budget allows -- more slices means narrower thumbnails, since slices x width is capped at 32768.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Thumbheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Thumbnail Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Height in pixels of each decoded thumbnail; width follows the movie aspect. The Animation editor zooms in hard, so a taller thumbnail is what stops the band going soft there -- 64 is fine for the timeline strip alone, 256 reads well zoomed. Costs decode time and memory, and needs a rebuild to take effect.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anfill
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Fill Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Stretch the filmstrip over the FULL height of the Animation editor. Works at any Thumbnail Height -- a low-resolution strip simply stretches, which is often fine for a faint background. Turn this off to confine the film to a band, sized by Graph Band Height.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anbandheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Band Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Height of the filmstrip band inside the Animation editor, in pixels, measured from the bottom. 0 fills the whole graph. This is a separate number from Strip Height because the two surfaces are different shapes: the timeline strip is a row added to a 70px bar, the graph is ~900px tall.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anshowmarks
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the marker lines in the Animation editor. Off stops the markers module rendering that view at all.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anmarkopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Marker Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How strongly the marker lines read in the Animation editor.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Decoder
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Decoder
FNS_TimelineTools.help:
Which decoder bakes the filmstrip.

Auto: try OpenCV, fall back to TouchDesigner if it cannot read the file.
OpenCV: fast (~2s) and off the main thread, but cannot read every format TD can.
TouchDesigner: reads anything TD can play, but costs one TD frame per movie frame (~90s for a 5300-frame file) and runs on the main thread.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Rebuildonstart
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Rebuild Strip On Start
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Bake the filmstrip and graph strip automatically when the project opens with media loaded. Unless Save Strip With Project is on, the bake lives in memory for the session only, so a reopened project shows an empty strip until Build is pressed -- or until this rebuilds it.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Savestrip
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Save Strip With Project
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Keep the baked thumbnails in the project file, so a reopened project shows the strip immediately without rebuilding. Costs several megabytes in the .toe (the full bake rides along in every save). Off: the bake lives in memory for the session only.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Build
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Build Strip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Capture the filmstrip now. Runs across frames; watch Status.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Clear
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Clear Strip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Drop the strip and stop the reader cooking.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Cancel
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Cancel Build
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Stop a build in progress. The TouchDesigner decoder can run for minutes, so it must be interruptible.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Backgroundstatus
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Background Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the background is doing -- layer levels, and the filmstrip build as it runs.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Points
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Resolution
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How many points the waveform is drawn with, spread across the whole file. Higher reads more detail when zoomed in and costs more GPU points.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Waveheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Wave Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Peak-to-peak height of the waveform as a fraction of the target surface's height. Held constant on screen while the graph zooms horizontally.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Wavecolor
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Wave Color
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Colour of the waveform line.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Waveopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Wave Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the waveform line over whatever it is drawn on.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Graphview
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Rendering Animation View
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Produce the Animation editor-shaped view. Driven by the background's layer switches -- a view nobody composites is not rendered at all.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Stripview
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Rendering Strip View
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Produce the timeline-strip-shaped view.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Fileoffset
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Start In File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Where in the audio file the timeline's working range opens, as a fraction. Non-zero whenever the range does not start at frame 1.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Filefraction
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Share of File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How much of the audio file the working range covers, as a fraction.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Spanfraction
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Span of Timeline
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How much of the working range the audio fills. Below 1 only when the file runs out before the range ends.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Waveformstatus
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Waveform Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the waveform tool is doing.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markerfile
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Marker list exported from an editor. Resolve marker EDL, Premiere marker CSV, Audacity/plain text labels, or FCPXML. The format is sniffed from the contents, not the extension.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Loadmarkers
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Load Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Re-read Marker File into the markers table.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Merge
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Merge On Load
FNS_TimelineTools.help: On: keep the markers already in the table and add the new ones, skipping duplicate times. Off: the file replaces the table.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Clearmarkers
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Clear Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Empty the markers table. The file on disk is untouched.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Refresh
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Refresh Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Re-map every marker onto the timeline and re-apply the look. Needed after the working range changes, since nothing downstream watches it.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Timebase
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Time Base
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What a marker time means. Timeline: seconds from the start of the working range -- works with no media loaded. Media: a position in the loaded media, mapped through the same offset and span the waveform uses, so markers stay stuck to the picture.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Sourcerate
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Source Frame Rate
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Frame rate of the TIMECODES IN THE FILE, used to turn HH:MM:SS:FF into seconds. 0 follows the scoped timeline. This never writes the timeline rate -- it only reads a file's.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Sourcestart
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Source Start Timecode
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Timecode the source sequence starts at, subtracted on import. "auto" floors the earliest marker to the whole hour, which is right for the 01:00:00:00 convention and a no-op for sequences starting at zero.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Exportformat
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Export Format
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Which format Save Markers writes. FNS CSV is this tool's own columns and loses nothing. Resolve EDL goes back into an edit, but only speaks the sixteen Resolve colour names -- anything else is snapped to the nearest and the status line says how many.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Exportfile
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Export File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Where Save Markers writes to.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Savemarkers
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Save Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Write the marker list out now.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markcolor
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Color
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Colour for markers whose file carries none. Premiere's CSV export has no colour field at all, so its markers all land here; Resolve names a colour per marker and that is kept.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlmarkwidth
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Width (Timeline)
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Line width in SCREEN pixels on the timeline strip. Held constant however far the Animation editor is zoomed.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anmarkwidth
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Width (Animation)
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Line width in SCREEN pixels in the Animation editor. Separate from the strip: the same pixel count is a bold rule on a 60px strip and a hairline across an 876px graph.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Share of the surface height a line covers, measured from the centre.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Labels
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Hover Labels
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the marker NAME when the mouse is over its line. Off draws no names at all. Names are hover-only rather than always-on because a row of them across a 60px strip overlaps into illegibility.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Labelsize
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Label Size
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Label height in SCREEN pixels. The strip renders wider than it is shown, so the horizontal size is compensated automatically -- this is the size you actually see.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Labelcolor
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Label Color
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Colour of the hover label.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markgraphview
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Render Graph View
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Produce the Animation editor-shaped view. Driven by the background's layer switches -- a view nobody composites is not rendered at all.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markstripview
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Render Strip View
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Produce the timeline-strip-shaped view.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markcount
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How many markers are in the table.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markerstatus
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the markers module last did.

FNS_Toolbar.name: Install
FNS_Toolbar.label: Install
FNS_Toolbar.help: Install the toolbar into TouchDesigner's UI now. It also installs on project start; this is the manual route after a change, or if the automatic install was skipped.

FNS_Toolbar.name: Layoutstart
FNS_Toolbar.label: Layout Start
FNS_Toolbar.help: The align-order the toolbar's first slot starts counting from. Each widget's position in the Def sequence is its own align order minus this, so it shifts the whole bar at once rather than moving anything relative to its neighbours.

FNS_Toolbar.name: Openauthor
FNS_Toolbar.label: Link
FNS_Toolbar.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Comp
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Widget COMP
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Panel COMP published as the toolbar widget. Defaults to the parent component.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Canonicalname
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Canonical Name
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Unique name for this widget in the global toolbar registry.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Callback
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Callback DAT
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Optional DAT with toolbar callbacks for this widget.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Autoregister
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Auto-register
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: When on, keep this widget published into the global toolbar registry while this component exists.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Register
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Register
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Publish once into the global toolbar registry, even if Auto-register is off.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Unregister
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Unregister
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Take this tool's contribution back out of the registry and turn Autoregister off, so it stays out. Register puts it back.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Regstatus
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Registration Status
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Read-only status of this host registration.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Menuorder
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Toolbar Order
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Preferred order among registered widgets, managed by the global registry. -1 = no preference (append at the end).

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Displayed
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Displayed
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Default visibility of the widget in the toolbar (managed by the global registry).

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Barwidth
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Bar Width
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Width of this widget in the toolbar. 0 = auto (follow the widget). Persisted here; the registry writes manager edits back.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Helpurl
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Help URL
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: The tool's wiki/help page opened from the Configurator (right-click the Name cell). Leave empty to auto-discover from a docsHelper COMP (its Url par) inside the registered panel or its parent.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Promotepars
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Promote Parameters
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: When on, the host mirrors its key Registration parameters onto the parent tool as a bound 'Registry' page. Turn off before shipping a tool that should not expose registry controls.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Presaveheal
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Pre-Save Heal
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Before each project save, re-check this registry: update entries whose component moved, drop entries whose component is gone, and republish a host that initialised before the global registry existed. Off skips the sweep for this registry only.

FNS_Updater.name: Baseurl
FNS_Updater.label: Base URL
FNS_Updater.help: Where the published manifest lives. Fetches <Base URL>/manifest.json; artifact URLs come from that manifest, pinned to their release. A local folder or file:// path works too, which is how the flow is exercised without a bucket.

FNS_Updater.name: Enabled
FNS_Updater.label: Enabled
FNS_Updater.help: Master switch for the Check and Update pulses.

FNS_Updater.name: Usediscovery
FNS_Updater.label: Use Discovery
FNS_Updater.help: Resolve the manifest location from the pinned discovery document instead of trusting Base URL. Leave on: it is what lets the bucket move without a component update, and it carries the minimum-version and notice channel. Turning it off pins this install to Base URL forever. A local or file:// Base URL always wins regardless.

FNS_Updater.name: Storefolder
FNS_Updater.label: Store Folder
FNS_Updater.help: Machine-wide package store the manifest and artifacts are fetched into. Blank means <user palette>/FNStools_ext/store.

FNS_Updater.name: Target
FNS_Updater.label: Target
FNS_Updater.help: The toolkit container whose packages are compared and updated.

FNS_Updater.name: Showprogress
FNS_Updater.label: Show Download Progress
FNS_Updater.help: Open the downloader's progress window while files are fetched.

FNS_Updater.name: Refreshstore
FNS_Updater.label: Refresh Store
FNS_Updater.help: Fetch the manifest and every artifact whose bytes differ into the store. Machine-wide: no project is touched.

FNS_Updater.name: Check
FNS_Updater.label: Check for Updates
FNS_Updater.help: Fetch the manifest and compare it against this project's install record. Cheap: no artifacts are downloaded.

FNS_Updater.name: Status
FNS_Updater.label: Status
FNS_Updater.help: Result of the last check, refresh or update pass.

FNS_Updater.name: Update
FNS_Updater.label: Update This Project
FNS_Updater.help: Fetch the artifacts this project needs and replace only the packages whose bytes differ. Never installs a package you did not choose.

FNS_Updater.name: Gateurl
FNS_Updater.label: Gate URL
FNS_Updater.help: Where entitlement is checked and gated packages are fetched from. Placeholder until the gate is deployed; it is the only address this component knows for paid downloads.

FNS_Updater.name: Signin
FNS_Updater.label: Sign In
FNS_Updater.help: Open your browser to sign in with Patreon. Nothing secret is stored in this project: the token lives in the operating system keystore, locked to this machine and this user.

FNS_Updater.name: Signout
FNS_Updater.label: Sign Out
FNS_Updater.help: Forget this machine's entitlement. Packages you already installed are untouched -- only future paid downloads stop.

FNS_Updater.name: Authstatus
FNS_Updater.label: Account
FNS_Updater.help: Who this install is signed in as and how many paid packages the account covers. Read-only.

FNS_Updater.name: Licensekey
FNS_Updater.label: Licence Key
FNS_Updater.help: A Gumroad licence key. Keys are per tool, so redeeming another one ADDS to this account rather than replacing it.

FNS_Updater.name: Licenseproduct
FNS_Updater.label: Licence Product
FNS_Updater.help: The Gumroad product id the key above belongs to. Shown on the product page you bought it from.

FNS_Updater.name: Redeemlicense
FNS_Updater.label: Redeem Licence
FNS_Updater.help: Check the licence key with the gate and add what it unlocks to this account.

FNS_Updater.name: Openauthor
FNS_Updater.label: Link
FNS_Updater.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

GlobalOutSelect.name: Refresh
GlobalOutSelect.label: Refresh
GlobalOutSelect.help: Rescan the project for global OP shortcuts and their out operators. The list is refreshed only on demand, so that walking the project never costs a frame while you work.

GlobalOutSelect.name: Openauthor
GlobalOutSelect.label: Link
GlobalOutSelect.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

GlobalVolControl.name: Volume
GlobalVolControl.label: Volume
GlobalVolControl.help: TouchDesigner's overall output volume, 0 to 1. This is the application-wide level, not a per-operator one.

GlobalVolControl.name: Mute
GlobalVolControl.label: Mute
GlobalVolControl.help: Silence TouchDesigner's audio output without losing the Volume setting.

GlobalVolControl.name: Openauthor
GlobalVolControl.label: Link
GlobalVolControl.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

HydroHomie.name: Enable
HydroHomie.label: Enable
HydroHomie.help: Turn the reminder on. Off by default -- with it off the component sits in the toolbar and never interrupts you.

HydroHomie.name: Intervalminutes
HydroHomie.label: Interval minutes
HydroHomie.help: Minutes between reminders. 45 by default; the countdown restarts when you click the alert away.

HydroHomie.name: Lfofreq
HydroHomie.label: LFO Freq
HydroHomie.help: How fast the alert icon pulses, in Hz. Lower is calmer; this only affects the animation, never the interval.

HydroHomie.name: Onstartactive
HydroHomie.label: On Start Active
HydroHomie.help: Start reminding as soon as the project opens, instead of waiting for Enable to be switched on by hand.

midiMapper.name: Id
midiMapper.label: Device ID
midiMapper.help: Which MIDI device the Reset button acts on. Middle-clicking the toolbar button resets every device instead.

midiMapper.name: Clear
midiMapper.label: Clear
midiMapper.help: Delete every mapping in the table below.

midiMapper.name: Learn
midiMapper.label: Learn
midiMapper.help: Listen for the next incoming MIDI message and assign it to the parameter you dropped on the UI. Turn it off when you are done assigning.

midiMapper.name: Edit
midiMapper.label: Edit Midimap DAT
midiMapper.help: Open the midimap table, where each row is one mapping and its min/max range.

midiMapper.name: Resetall
midiMapper.label: Reset All Midi
midiMapper.help: Bypass and un-bypass every MIDI operator to unstick a device that has stopped responding.

midiMapper.name: Resetdelayms
midiMapper.label: Reset Delay (Ms)
midiMapper.help: How long to leave the MIDI operators bypassed during a reset, in milliseconds. Raise it if a device needs longer to let go of the port.

midiMapper.name: Mappingtablerepositorie
midiMapper.label: Mappingtable
midiMapper.help: The table DAT holding the mappings. Point it at another table to keep mappings somewhere else -- in a shared component, for instance.

midiMapper.name: Mappingtablecreate
midiMapper.label: Create
midiMapper.help: Create a mapping table and point the parameter above at it.

OpenExt.name: Openauthor
OpenExt.label: Link
OpenExt.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

OpenExt.name: Shortcuts
OpenExt.label: Shortcuts
OpenExt.help: Key that opens the selected COMP's promoted extension in your external editor. The default is an expression that picks the right keys per platform -- typing a plain value over it pins the tool to one OS.

OpTemplates.name: Target
OpTemplates.label: Root
OpTemplates.help: The component whose network is watched for newly created operators. '/' watches the whole project; narrow it if you want templates to apply in one branch only.

OpTemplates.name: External
OpTemplates.label: External Templates Sync
OpTemplates.help: Keep the templates in their own .tox in your user palette folder instead of inside the project file, so the same templates follow you into every project. Switching it on writes that file, and asks first if one of that name already exists.

OpTemplates.name: Advanced
OpTemplates.label: Advanced
OpTemplates.help: Reveal the two controls below, which point the tool at a different templates component. Leave it off unless you are keeping more than one set.

OpTemplates.name: Createtemplates
OpTemplates.label: Create Templates
OpTemplates.help: Create a fresh templates component and point the tool at it.

OpTemplates.name: Templates
OpTemplates.label: Templates
OpTemplates.help: The component holding your template definitions -- one Base COMP per OP type, named after that type.

OpTemplates.name: Opentemplates
OpTemplates.label: Open Templates
OpTemplates.help: Open the templates component in a floating network, to add or edit templates by hand.

OpTemplates.name: Savetemplates
OpTemplates.label: Save Templates
OpTemplates.help: Write the templates to disk: to the external .tox when External is on, otherwise by saving the project. It confirms first, because it overwrites what is already there.

OpTemplates.name: Refreshtemplates
OpTemplates.label: Refresh Templates
OpTemplates.help: Reload the templates component from its external .tox, discarding unsaved edits made in this session.

OpTemplates.name: Keys
OpTemplates.label: Keys
OpTemplates.help: The modifier keys held to trigger this gesture, space-separated (TouchDesigner key names). The default is an expression that picks the right keys per platform -- typing a plain value over it pins the tool to one OS.

OpTemplates.name: Openauthor
OpTemplates.label: Link
OpTemplates.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

OpToClipboard.name: Active
OpToClipboard.label: Active
OpToClipboard.help: Turn OpToClipboard on or off. When on, the copy shortcut puts the selected operator's reference on the clipboard ready to paste into an expression. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

OpToClipboard.name: Shortcut
OpToClipboard.label: Shortcut
OpToClipboard.help: Hotkey that copies the selected operator's reference to the clipboard.

OpToClipboard.name: Openauthor
OpToClipboard.label: Link
OpToClipboard.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

oscMapper.name: Clear
oscMapper.label: Clear
oscMapper.help: Delete every mapping in the table below.

oscMapper.name: Learn
oscMapper.label: Learn
oscMapper.help: Listen for the next incoming OSC message and assign it to the parameter you dropped on the UI. Turn it off when you are done assigning.

oscMapper.name: Edit
oscMapper.label: Edit DAT
oscMapper.help: Open the mapping table, where each row is one mapping and its min/max range.

oscMapper.name: Active
oscMapper.label: Active
oscMapper.help: Receive OSC. Off closes the listening port and leaves the mappings untouched.

oscMapper.name: Protocol
oscMapper.label: Protocol
oscMapper.help: The OSC transport to listen on. Messaging is the ordinary one; multicast receives from a group address, and reliable adds delivery guarantees at the cost of latency. It must match what the sender uses.

oscMapper.name: Port
oscMapper.label: Port
oscMapper.help: The UDP port to receive OSC on. It must match the port the sender transmits to.

oscMapper.name: Addscope
oscMapper.label: OSC Address Scope
oscMapper.help: Which OSC addresses to accept, as a pattern -- '*' takes everything. Narrow it when several tools share one port.

oscMapper.name: Localaddress
oscMapper.label: Local Address
oscMapper.help: Which network interface to listen on. Empty means all of them; set it on a machine with several network cards.

oscMapper.name: Active2
oscMapper.label: Talkback Active
oscMapper.help: Send values back out over OSC as they change, so a controller with motorised faders or LEDs can follow TouchDesigner.

oscMapper.name: Address
oscMapper.label: Network Address
oscMapper.help: The host talkback is sent to. 127.0.0.1 stays on this machine; use the controller's IP to reach it over the network.

oscMapper.name: Localaddress2
oscMapper.label: Local Address
oscMapper.help: Which network interface talkback is sent from. '*' lets the OS choose.

oscMapper.name: Port2
oscMapper.label: Port
oscMapper.help: The UDP port talkback is sent to. It must match the port the receiving device listens on, and is normally not the port above.

oscMapper.name: Mappingtablerepositorie
oscMapper.label: Mappingtable
oscMapper.help: The table DAT holding the mappings. Point it at another table to keep mappings somewhere else -- in a shared component, for instance.

oscMapper.name: Mappingtablecreate
oscMapper.label: Create
oscMapper.help: Create a mapping table and point the parameter above at it.

OUTPUT.name: Performwindow
OUTPUT.label: Perform Window
OUTPUT.help: The Window COMP these tools drive. Dropping an operator on the toolbar button sets that window's Window Operator, and the streaming switches below follow the same window.

OUTPUT.name: Spoutactive
OUTPUT.label: Spout Active
OUTPUT.help: Stream the perform window to other applications on this machine over Spout (Windows) or Syphon (macOS).

OUTPUT.name: Sendername
OUTPUT.label: Sender Name
OUTPUT.help: The name other applications see this Spout/Syphon stream under. Change it when two TouchDesigner instances would otherwise publish the same name.

OUTPUT.name: Ndiactive
OUTPUT.label: NDI Active
OUTPUT.help: Stream the perform window over NDI, so machines on the same network can receive it.

OUTPUT.name: Name
OUTPUT.label: NDI Source Name
OUTPUT.help: The NDI source name this machine publishes. It is what receivers pick from their source list, so make it identifiable when several machines are streaming.

ParOPDrop.name: Active
ParOPDrop.label: Active
ParOPDrop.help: Turn ParOPDrop on or off. When on, dragging a custom parameter onto the toolbar button (or pressing its hotkey over one) creates the matching Par CHOP, Par DAT or ParExec DAT inside the COMP. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

ParOPDrop.name: Keys
ParOPDrop.label: Key
ParOPDrop.help: Key held to drop an operator reference onto a parameter. Modifiers are ignored.

ParOPDrop.name: Openauthor
ParOPDrop.label: Link
ParOPDrop.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

ParRandomizer.name: Active
ParRandomizer.label: Active
ParRandomizer.help: Turn ParRandomizer on or off. When on, the toolbar button, drag-and-drop and the shortcuts below randomize parameters. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

ParRandomizer.name: Shortcutop
ParRandomizer.label: Shortcut Randomize OP
ParRandomizer.help: Key that randomizes every value slider on the selected operator.

ParRandomizer.name: Shortcutpar
ParRandomizer.label: Shortcut Randomize Rollover Par
ParRandomizer.help: Key that randomizes just the parameter the mouse is over.

ParRandomizer.name: Shortcutreset
ParRandomizer.label: Shortcut Reset Parameter
ParRandomizer.help: Key that puts the parameter under the mouse back to its default.

ParRandomizer.name: Shortcutresetallcustom
ParRandomizer.label: Shortcut Reset All Custom
ParRandomizer.help: Key that puts every parameter on the hovered parameter's page back to its default.

ParRandomizer.name: Openauthor
ParRandomizer.label: Link
ParRandomizer.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

paste_from_clipboard.name: Pasteimage
paste_from_clipboard.label: Paste Image
paste_from_clipboard.help: Paste image from clipboard as TOP

paste_from_clipboard.name: Pastescriptop
paste_from_clipboard.label: Paste As ScriptOP
paste_from_clipboard.help: Paste image from clipboard as a scriptTOP

paste_from_clipboard.name: Pasteannotate
paste_from_clipboard.label: Paste As Note
paste_from_clipboard.help: Paste image from clipboard as an annotate component

paste_from_clipboard.name: Shortcut
paste_from_clipboard.label: Shortcut
paste_from_clipboard.help: Key that pastes the image on your clipboard into the current network. Once pressed, 1 / 2 / 3 choose Movie File In, locked Script TOP or Annotate.

paste_from_clipboard.name: Positionatmouse
paste_from_clipboard.label: Position at Mouse
paste_from_clipboard.help: Position image at current mouse location

paste_from_clipboard.name: Status
paste_from_clipboard.label: Status
paste_from_clipboard.help: What the tool is doing, or why it cannot: read-only. It reports the Windows-only limitation here rather than failing silently on macOS.

paste_from_clipboard.name: Bypass
paste_from_clipboard.label: Bypass
paste_from_clipboard.help: Switch the whole component off. It is set automatically on anything but Windows, where the clipboard route this tool uses does not exist.

paste_from_clipboard.name: Showbuiltin
paste_from_clipboard.label: Show Built-in Parameters
paste_from_clipboard.help: Show TouchDesigner's built-in parameter pages on this component alongside its custom ones. Off keeps the parameter dialog to just this tool's own controls.

paste_from_clipboard.name: Chattd
paste_from_clipboard.label: ChatTD Operator
paste_from_clipboard.help: Optional: a ChatTD operator for this component to talk to. Leave it empty unless you use DotSimulate's ChatTD.

QuickCollapse.name: Active
QuickCollapse.label: Active
QuickCollapse.help: Turn QuickCollapse on or off. When on, the shortcuts below collapse the selected nodes into a Base COMP. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

QuickCollapse.name: Shortcut
QuickCollapse.label: Shortcut
QuickCollapse.help: Key that collapses the selected nodes into a new Base COMP straight away, with no dialog.

QuickCollapse.name: Shortcutcustomize
QuickCollapse.label: Shortcut Customize
QuickCollapse.help: Key that collapses the selection but asks first -- a dialog for the new COMP's name and its parent shortcut.

QuickCollapse.name: Openauthor
QuickCollapse.label: Link
QuickCollapse.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

QuickMarks.name: Active
QuickMarks.label: Active
QuickMarks.help: Turn QuickMarks on or off. When on, the number-key shortcuts save, recall and remove marks; the marks themselves are kept in the project file either way. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

QuickMarks.name: Shortcuts
QuickMarks.label: Shortcuts
QuickMarks.help: Hotkeys for storing and recalling marks. Character classes such as [0-9] expand.

QuickMarks.name: Mark
QuickMarks.label: Quickmarks
QuickMarks.help: One block per quickmark slot. Block N is the slot reached by ctrl+N, so the first ten line up with the hotkeys; extra blocks are reachable by command only.

QuickMarks.name: Mark0name
QuickMarks.label: Name
QuickMarks.help: Your label for this quickmark. Free text, shown in the command palette. Editing it never affects where the mark points.

QuickMarks.name: Mark0data
QuickMarks.label: Data
QuickMarks.help: The stored location as JSON (network, current child, pan x/y, zoom). Written by Store; edit only if you know the shape.

QuickMarks.name: Migrated
QuickMarks.label: Migrated From Storage
QuickMarks.help: Set once the slots have been copied out of the legacy StorageManager into this sequence. The old storage is left in place untouched as a one-time backup; nothing reads it after migration.

QuickMarks.name: Help
QuickMarks.label: Help
QuickMarks.help: Open this tool's documentation page in your browser.

QuickPane.name: Active
QuickPane.label: Active
QuickPane.help: Turn QuickPane on or off. When on, holding the modifier and dragging from a selected COMP splits the pane in that direction and navigates into it. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

QuickPane.name: Ratio
QuickPane.label: Ratio Horz/Vert
QuickPane.help: How much of the pane the new split takes, 0-1: the first value for a horizontal split, the second for a vertical one.

QuickPane.name: Keys
QuickPane.label: Keys
QuickPane.help: The modifier keys held to trigger this gesture, space-separated (TouchDesigner key names). The default is an expression that picks the right keys per platform -- typing a plain value over it pins the tool to one OS.

QuickPane.name: Shortcuts
QuickPane.label: Pane Shortcuts
QuickPane.help: Hotkeys that split and navigate panes. Separate from Keys, which is the held-modifier set.

QuickPane.name: Openauthor
QuickPane.label: Link
QuickPane.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

QuickTime.name: Multiplier
QuickTime.label: Multiplier
QuickTime.help: Scales the absTime and absFrame references QuickTime hands out: 1 is real time, 0.5 runs them at half speed.

QuickTime.name: Reset
QuickTime.label: Reset
QuickTime.help: Set QuickTime's internal timers back to zero. Middle-clicking the toolbar icon does the same thing.

QuickTime.name: Openauthor
QuickTime.label: Link
QuickTime.help: Open the author's page in your browser.

ResetPLS1.name: Root
ResetPLS1.label: Root
ResetPLS1.help: Where the search for resettable operators starts. Everything under this component is considered, subject to Depth and the exception lists.

ResetPLS1.name: Limitdepth
ResetPLS1.label: Limit Depth
ResetPLS1.help: Stop the search at a fixed number of levels below Root instead of walking the whole tree. Worth it in a big project where a full walk is slow.

ResetPLS1.name: Depth
ResetPLS1.label: Depth
ResetPLS1.help: How many levels below Root to search, when Limit Depth is on.

ResetPLS1.name: Except
ResetPLS1.label: Except
ResetPLS1.help: Operators to leave alone, one pattern per entry. Everything else under Root is reset.

ResetPLS1.name: Exceptionslimit
ResetPLS1.label: Exceptions Limit
ResetPLS1.help: For an excepted COMP, also skip everything inside it. Off resets its children even though the COMP itself is excepted.

ResetPLS1.name: Enableall
ResetPLS1.label: Enable All OPtypes
ResetPLS1.help: Switch on every operator-type toggle across the pages, so the reset covers everything this tool knows how to reset.

ResetPLS1.name: Disableall
ResetPLS1.label: Disable All OPtypes
ResetPLS1.help: Switch off every operator-type toggle, so the reset covers nothing until you pick types back.

ResetPLS1.name: Resetonstartup
ResetPLS1.label: Reset On Startup
ResetPLS1.help: Fire the reset once, automatically, when the project opens.

ResetPLS1.name: Reset
ResetPLS1.label: Reset
ResetPLS1.help: Reset now: pulse the reset parameter of every included operator under Root. This is what the hotkey and the toolbar button do.

ResetPLS1.name: Shortcut
ResetPLS1.label: Reset Shortcut
ResetPLS1.help: Hotkey that pulses Global ResetPLS. Both the Windows and macOS combos are listed.

ResetPLS1.name: Feedbacktop
ResetPLS1.label: Feedback
ResetPLS1.help: Include Feedback TOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Cachetop
ResetPLS1.label: Cache
ResetPLS1.help: Include Cache TOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Texture3d
ResetPLS1.label: Texture 3D
ResetPLS1.help: Include Texture 3D TOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Moviefilein
ResetPLS1.label: Movie File In
ResetPLS1.help: Include Movie File In TOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Flow
ResetPLS1.label: Flow
ResetPLS1.help: Include Flow TOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Blobtrack
ResetPLS1.label: Blob Track
ResetPLS1.help: Include Blob Track TOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Scripttop
ResetPLS1.label: Script
ResetPLS1.help: Include Script TOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else. Reset here means pulsing a custom parameter named Reset or Resetpulse -- the list of names it looks for is editable under Misc, Edit Custom Reset Pars.

ResetPLS1.name: Lfo
ResetPLS1.label: LFO
ResetPLS1.help: Include LFO CHOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Speed
ResetPLS1.label: Speed
ResetPLS1.help: Include Speed CHOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Count
ResetPLS1.label: Count
ResetPLS1.help: Include Count CHOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Timer
ResetPLS1.label: Timer
ResetPLS1.help: Include Timer CHOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Filter
ResetPLS1.label: Filter
ResetPLS1.help: Include Filter CHOPs in the reset sweep, so their reset parameter is pulsed along with everything else.

ResetPLS1.name: Lag
ResetPLS1.label: Lag

about_stamp.help: The package's own version, governed by us -- bump it whenever you change this package. It is what tells an install that a newer build exists: the manifest publishes it and the updater compares it against this parameter on the installed component. Artifact hashes cannot answer that (a .tox re-exports to different bytes every time), so nothing else does.
